chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of our companions, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Musa ibn Ukeyl al-Numayri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who is traveling and has a knife in his sock, which he cannot do without, or tied in his trousers, and a key he fears losing, or a belt in his waist containing iron. He said: There is no problem with the knife and the belt for the traveler during a time of necessity, and similarly the key he fears losing or is in forgetfulness; and there is no problem with the sword, and similarly the weapon in war; but in other cases, prayer is not permissible in anything of iron, for it is unclean and transformed.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray while wearing iron items like a belt or knife?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while iron is generally considered *najis* (ritually impure) and *mamsukh* (transformed), making prayer invalid if worn, exceptions are made for travelers carrying essential items like knives, keys, or belts out of necessity or forgetfulness. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of *darura* (necessity) overriding general prohibitions, ensuring that practical needs do not invalidate worship. The distinction between general prohibition and specific necessity underscores the flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding ritual purity in dynamic contexts.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from one of our companions, from Ali BinUqba, from Musa Bin Akeyl Al Nameyri, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked himasws about the man who happens to be in the journey, and with him is a knife in his socks or in his trouser, not being able to do without it, tightened, and the key he is fearing upon losing it, or in his waist is the belt wherein is iron. Heasws said: ‘There is no problem with the knife and the belt for the traveller during a time of desperation, and similar to that is the key he is fearing upon, or regarding forgetfulness; and there is no problem with the sword, and similar to that is the reason for the weapon during the war etc. The Salāt is not allowed during anything from the iron, for it is unclean, transformed’.
en.sarwar: 13. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from certain persons of our people from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah from Musa ibn ‘Ukayl al-Numayriy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who on a journey has a knife in his slipper without which he cannot do anything or it is in his pant, and a key which he is afraid of losing it, or that around his midsection is a belt in which there is iron. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not an offense to have a knife, or a belt for a traveler in case he needs them as well as a key for which one is afraid about forgetting it. It is not an offense to have a sword or weapons during a war and in other times. It is not permissible to perform Salah (prayer) with iron; it is Najis (unclean) and metamorphosed. ’ ”
